doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Composing for the Mills College orchestra and Conversations CDs
summary: Mitchell founded a chamber orchestra at Mills College, recorded with Wide Hive, and transcribed improvisations with Craig Taborn and Kikanju Baku into orchestral pieces.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I can recall sort of a realization as I was listening to jazz back when I was about your age and starting to sort out the way the music worked, the accompanist, the soloist, maybe starting to realize about song form. Do you recall that sort of realization coming to you?

Well yeah and I took that even further I mean you know ‘cause I’m a composer as well. So I have several pieces and CDs and so on that I’ve put out with the orchestra that I founded when I was teaching at Mills College you know. So yeah, let’s see hold it, I’ve lost my thought for a minute — I’ve got out several CDs of this — and one of my CDs

won the New York Times Award of the Year. And the thing about it is that what I did was went out to Mills College and put together my own 36-piece chamber orchestra and then recorded them all. I work with Gregory Howe of Wide Hive Records, a man that was wide open to new ideas and so on and so forth. My CDs “Conversations” numbers 1 and 2 with Craig Taborn and Kikanju Baku I transcribed our improvisations and turned those into like pieces for orchestra. And that gave me a chance to work on improvisation in another whole way where I was able to actually sit down and look at a transcription and then keep on you know taking the next steps in orchestrating it. So and that taught me a lot about how things work. But it doesn’t stop there because it gave me the chance to — I already was experiencing doing it in real time, so it gave me the chance to experience it, you know, in another form where I could actually keep working on it. So yeah, I tend to study opposites, you know, because that helps me figure out like what’s going on in the middle.

Yes I remember reading that quote from you and I thought it was very interesting, and then you had also said, “If you’re sitting at home composing you’ve got time but what you want to get yourself to the point to where you can make these decisions spontaneously.” In the context you were talking about the super musician.
